label: Quadratic Functions
overview: A quadratic function f(x) = ax² + bx + c produces a parabola. SAT questions ask you to identify the vertex, axis of symmetry, x-intercepts (zeros), and y-intercept; convert between standard, vertex, and factored forms; and interpret these features in context. The sign of a tells you whether the parabola opens up (a > 0) or down (a < 0).

keyFormulas.name: Vertex form
keyFormulas.latex: f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k \quad \text{vertex at } (h, k)

keyFormulas.name: Factored form
keyFormulas.latex: f(x) = a(x - r_1)(x - r_2) \quad \text{zeros at } r_1, r_2

workedExamples.problem: For f(x) = x² − 4x + 3, find the vertex and zeros.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing vertex form h and k signs: f(x) = (x + 3)² + 1 has vertex (3, 1)
commonMistakes.fix: In f(x) = a(x − h)² + k, the vertex is at (h, k). Since (x + 3) = (x − (−3)), h = −3, not +3.

commonMistakes.mistake: Thinking a > 0 means the vertex is a maximum
commonMistakes.fix: When a > 0 the parabola opens upward, so the vertex is a MINIMUM. It's a maximum only when a < 0.

quickTip: To quickly convert standard form to vertex form, complete the square or use x = −b/(2a) to find h, then plug back in to get k. Knowing all three forms (standard, vertex, factored) and when to use each one is the whole skill.
